how: Members repeat a flag call, recall an earlier suggestion with little luck and invite helpers to a build already started with friends.
The revised role covers proposing and beginning the flag without requiring proof that other builders joined a particular starter.
The members propose a flag as their mark without a visible design deliberation.
Members report starting the flag and announce collective presence on the canvas.
A plan and coordinate links make the build findable to helpers.
Members share a coordination server during building and later seek renewed access after its invite expires.
Access to an existing coordination chat requires renewal when its invitation expires, including after canvas placement has ended.
The builder identifies a good site and plans work across a neighbouring sign without describing a loss that forced this choice.
The neighbour proposes coexistence and the builder refuses because the flag extends downward, so negotiation does not settle a border.
A member announces planned encroachment across a neighbouring sign without establishing actual destruction or a coordinated raid.
Members celebrate success, congratulate the builders and praise the group despite its narrow remaining result.
The congratulatory reply also records that about five pixels remained.
The affected neighbour responds to announced encroachment with a deal request, but the builder refuses rather than accepting a truce.
The same builder's announcement precedes their later success declaration without establishing that the report caused collective celebration.
A reply to the success declaration combines praise with a fate report without establishing a motive to preserve the work.
The observed recruitment reply requests help rather than giving bare acceptance, while later congratulations answer success rather than a call.
Little luck and a narrow remaining result do not establish a prior judgement of insufficient hands or room.
Regretting missed participation does not establish withdrawal under strain or repair of an internal quarrel.
A plan and location invitation do not establish a question about canvas rules or pictures and its explanation.
Visible friend-group coordination cannot establish whether organizational decisions were absent from the unseen chat or assess a cross-room frequency claim.
The plan and chat references do not decide whether machines or spare accounts placed pixels.
The server invitation and local-language build announcement do not establish secrecy, infiltration or deliberate concealment from rivals.
Missing notice of the build and spending a day in chat do not establish placing around obligations, device limits or personal costs.
An expired chat invitation does not establish a canvas fault or a placing workaround.
The remaining-pixels account describes neither maintenance nor keepers repairing an agreed change away before learning of it.
The fate report identifies neither who changed the work nor why.
Different early and later locations do not establish a move caused by loss of an earlier site.
The builder refuses coexistence in the observed pair, establishing scoped non-restraint without deciding what happened elsewhere.
The answer states spatial limits of the design rather than limits of authority to commit the group.
The visitor identifies as a group member without establishing an envoy role carrying proposals between venues.
Identifying with the neighbouring group does not establish membership of both sides or divided allegiance.
The overlap exchange does not describe a host ruling over guest artwork.
The coexistence proposal and spatial refusal do not show help exchanged between groups.
A coordination-server invitation alone does not establish an inter-room coalition.
The disagreement concerns whether the designs fit without arguing whether covering the neighbour is fair.
A flag proposal does not establish politics, lore, belonging or colour faith beyond representation through the mark.
The named canvas neighbour is not described as a rival from a prior quarrel.
The encroachment announcement gives no inherited tie as its reason.
The success declaration and praise do not establish a new canvas joke.
Sharing and using a chat do not establish a new room forming around the mark.
The spatial refusal contains no dispute about offensive jokes, words or hate symbols.
The flag call and location announcement do not establish a host-sub April Fools performance.
The flag call and chat invitation do not establish host containment of canvas talk.
Planned encroachment on a neighbour does not establish host members attacking their own work because of canvas posts.
Renewed chat access after the close does not reveal a decision about a future collective purpose.
Reporting remaining pixels does not establish a contest over cleanup or which account of the event is retained.
The visiting neighbour does not say the mark brought them into ordinary community participation.
Congratulating the builders does not establish outreach to creators, press or people beyond the canvas.
The success declaration names no defeated rival or continuing contest in talk.
The later reply reports an existing build, leaving the earlier call's recruiting effect unresolved.
Starting with friends and calling for help occur in one report, leaving the proposed causal order unresolved.
The result report cannot establish whether building produced maintenance activity.
The coexistence request does not establish upkeep as the trigger for border talk.
The observed proposal is refused, so no settled border is available to produce restraint in that exchange.
The remaining-pixels report cannot establish upkeep causing a turn to machine placement.
The build-to-success sequence does not isolate the proposed mechanism whereby a finished report prompts collective celebration.
The reply links success and fate reporting but does not establish a motive to preserve the work.
The fate report and later invite request do not establish recording causing a future-purpose decision.
Little luck and a later site do not establish insufficient hands causing relocation.
Sharing a plan does not establish that it settled a design argument.
The written build report asks for help, while acceptance through placing leaves no observable answer here.
The negotiation exchange does not establish maintenance strain producing outside help.
The failed accommodation exchange does not establish border talk producing exchanged help.
The earlier invitation and later encroachment announcement do not establish recruitment directing the later builder into attack.
The observed overlap exchange ends in the builder's spatial refusal rather than restraint, without deciding conduct elsewhere.
The success declaration does not identify a rival contest arising from the earlier encroachment.
Sharing a coordination chat does not establish maintenance producing an inter-room coalition.
The invitation and server link do not establish recruitment flooding the host and causing containment.
The observed pair reaches no agreement or authority question, so the bounded after-agreement mechanism is unnecessary for explaining its spatial refusal.
